q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT DISTINCT A.CUSTOMER_ID AS CUSTOMER_ID FROM (SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) AS NUM_PRODUCTS FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID)A JOIN (SELECT COUNT(PRODUCT_KEY) AS NUM_PRODUCTS FROM PRODUCT)B ON(A.NUM_PRODUCTS = B.NUM_PRODUCTS) WHERE A.CUSTOMER_ID IS NOT NULL

counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1), (2); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1, 1), (1, 2), (2, 1);
explanation: Q1 checks if the number of distinct products purchased by any customer is equal to the total number of distinct products. Q2 checks if there exists at least one customer who has purchased all distinct products. The difference lies in the quantification of the condition: Q1 uses an equality check, while Q2 uses an existence check.
counterexample_dsp: A test database with 2 products and 2 customers, where customer 1 has purchased both products, and customer 2 has purchased only one product. This triggers the difference because Q1 returns customer 1, while Q2 does not return any customer.
